title: Portable Appliance Testing
subtitle: Five Portable Appliance Testing practice mocks
description: Five Portable Appliance Testing practice mocks covering equipment classes, visual inspection, combined testing, detachable leads, records, limits and practical judgement.
format: Five rotating practice mocks: three 50-question tests, one 30-question test and one 35-question homework paper. Exam format: 80 minutes, open book. Pass at 80%+.

questions.prompt: Class I equipment:
questions.explanation: Class I equipment relies on basic insulation plus a protective earth connection. The exposed conductive parts must be earthed so a fault current can operate the protective device.

questions.prompt: The most important check, when assessing the level of safety of an electrical appliance, is:
questions.explanation: Visual inspection is the most important check because many dangerous faults are visible before testing. Damaged plugs, cords, cases and misuse are often found this way.

questions.prompt: A flexible cord connected to a 650 W iron should be protected by a fuse rating of:
questions.explanation: A 650 W load at 230 V draws about 2.8 A. The next suitable standard BS 1362 plug fuse is 3 A.

questions.prompt: Equipment users should be competent to inspect:
questions.explanation: Users are expected to spot obvious external defects in accessible equipment and outlets. They should not dismantle equipment, but they can identify damaged or scorched socket outlets.

questions.prompt: Instrument test leads should comply with
questions.explanation: HSE Guidance Note GS 38 sets safety requirements for test leads and probes. It is especially relevant where voltage measurements above extra-low voltage may be made.

questions.prompt: The maximum permitted length of a 1.25 mm² extension lead fitted with a standard 13 A plug should not exceed:
questions.explanation: Extension lead length is limited to keep earth loop impedance and volt drop within acceptable limits. For a 1.25 mm² lead on a 13 A plug, the maximum is 12 m.

questions.prompt: Equipment with an earth leakage current exceeding 3.5 mA shall:

options.A: Be permanently wired or supplied by a plug and socket to BS 4343 (BS EN 6030-2)
options.B: Have a label indicating the value of leakage current
options.C: Have protective conductors of not less than 0.5 mm²
options.D: Only be used in commercial situations

questions.explanation: Equipment with leakage above 3.5 mA needs a more secure protective conductor arrangement. Permanent wiring or an industrial plug-and-socket helps ensure the earth path cannot be casually disconnected.

questions.prompt: When carrying out an insulation resistance test on a Class I household portable appliance to BS 3456 using the earth leakage method, the maximum acceptable value is:
questions.explanation: The earth leakage method checks the current that would flow to earth in normal use. For this Class I household appliance case, the accepted maximum is 0.75 mA.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following domestic electrical appliances may be regarded as an item of stationary equipment:
questions.explanation: A washing machine is normally placed in one position and not moved during use. That makes it stationary rather than handheld, portable or transportable.

questions.prompt: An item of stationary equipment is defined as not having a carrying handle and having a mass greater than:
questions.explanation: Stationary equipment is not fitted with a carrying handle and is too heavy to be moved easily. The mass threshold used here is greater than 18 kg.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following would not normally be part of a user inspection:

options.A: Checking security of the flexible cable in its plug top
options.B: Checking the connections within the plug
options.C: Looking for signs of external damage to the equipment
options.D: Operating to check that it works properly

questions.explanation: A user inspection is external and does not normally involve opening the plug. Checking internal plug connections belongs to a formal visual inspection by a competent person.

questions.prompt: Class II equipment has an identifying mark in the shape of:

options.C: Two circles, one inside the other
options.D: Two squares, one inside the other

questions.explanation: Class II equipment is identified by the double-square symbol. The mark shows that protection is by double or reinforced insulation, not by an earth connection.

questions.prompt: New 13A plugs manufactured to BS 1363 will have:
questions.explanation: New BS 1363 plugs have sleeved line and neutral pins. The partial insulation reduces the risk of touching live metal while the plug is being inserted or withdrawn.

questions.prompt: When conducting an earth continuity test on IT equipment:

options.A: All IT equipment in the area must be disconnected
options.B: Permission should first be sought from the equipment user
options.C: The equipment casing should be removed
options.D: The equipment must be connected to the mains

questions.explanation: Testing IT equipment can interrupt use, risk data loss or affect sensitive electronics. Permission from the user should be obtained before carrying out the earth continuity test.

questions.prompt: Electrical equipment for use in domestic environments will normally be fitted with a 13A plug manufactured to:
questions.explanation: The normal domestic 13 A plug is made to BS 1363. That standard covers the plug construction and fuse arrangement used in UK homes.

questions.prompt: A 20 metre 1.5 mm² extension lead should be protected by:
questions.explanation: A 20 m, 1.5 mm² extension lead is longer than the usual 15 m limit for that size. The fuse protects the flex, and the RCD gives additional shock protection for the extended lead.

questions.prompt: A flexible cord connected to equipment having an electrical rating of 800 W should normally be protected by a fuse rating of:
questions.explanation: An 800 W appliance draws about 3.5 A at 230 V. The next suitable standard plug fuse above the normal load is 5 A.

questions.prompt: When a standard 13A plug overheats the cause would most likely be due to:

options.A: A loose connection within the plug
options.D: The use of socket outlets not to BS Standards

questions.explanation: A loose terminal creates high resistance at the connection. Under load that resistance produces heat, which is why plugs often overheat at poor connections.

questions.prompt: The minimum acceptable insulation resistance for Class I heating equipment rated greater than 3 kW is:
questions.explanation: Large heating elements can naturally give lower insulation readings than other Class I equipment. For Class I heating equipment above 3 kW, the minimum accepted value here is 0.3 megohms.

questions.prompt: Electrical equipment should be marked with a unique serial number to help:
questions.explanation: A unique serial or asset number links the appliance to its inspection history and records. Without identification, results cannot reliably be tied to the right item.

questions.prompt: Earth continuity testing may sometimes be carried out using:
questions.explanation: A low resistance ohmmeter can verify continuity of the protective conductor where that method is suitable. It measures small resistance values in the earth path.

questions.prompt: A BS 3535 safety isolating transformer having a voltage not exceeding 50 V is used to supply certain equipment complying with:
questions.explanation: Class III equipment is protected by supply at separated extra-low voltage. A BS 3535 safety isolating transformer up to 50 V provides that type of supply.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not normally form a part of in-service testing:
questions.explanation: Loop testing is a fixed-installation test, not a normal in-service appliance test. PAT focuses on appliance inspection, continuity, insulation/leakage and functional checks.

questions.prompt: Electrical equipment users should be:

options.D: Capable of inspecting equipment for obvious defects

questions.explanation: Users are not expected to dismantle equipment or carry out instrument tests. They should be capable of noticing obvious damage or unsafe condition before use.

questions.prompt: The test current applied to electric equipment fitted with a 13A plug fuse, during an earth continuity test, would normally be:

options.C: 25A for a period between 5 and 20 seconds

questions.explanation: For equipment protected by a 13 A plug fuse, the high-current earth continuity test is normally 25 A for 5 to 20 seconds. This proves the protective conductor and its terminations can carry fault current.

questions.prompt: The recommended initial frequency of user checks, relevant to a children's ride in the entrance of a store, could be:
questions.explanation: A children's ride in a store entrance is frequently used and used by a vulnerable group. Daily user checks are a sensible initial frequency for obvious damage or misuse.

questions.prompt: Identification of electrical equipment within a duty holder's control is required to produce:
questions.explanation: The duty holder needs to know which items are under control before inspection intervals and records can be managed. Identification feeds directly into the equipment register.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does not apply when testing on a two-core cord set:
questions.explanation: A two-core cord set has no protective conductor. Because there is no earth conductor, an earth continuity test is not applicable.

questions.prompt: Class I equipment with internal electronic components should be tested with a current not greater than:
questions.explanation: Sensitive Class I electronic equipment should not be stressed with a high continuity current. A low-current test not greater than 200 mA reduces the risk of damage.

questions.prompt: It should be confirmed, when carrying out a formal visual inspection, that electrical equipment is being operated:

options.A: As laid down in the manufacturer's instructions

questions.explanation: Formal visual inspection includes checking that the equipment is suitable and being used correctly. Manufacturer's instructions define the intended operating conditions.

questions.prompt: When protection against electric shock from equipment is provided using an earth wire, the equipment classification would be:
questions.explanation: If shock protection depends on an earth wire, the appliance is Class I. The protective conductor provides the fault path for exposed metal parts.

questions.prompt: User checks of stationary equipment in industrial premises should be carried out:
questions.explanation: Stationary equipment in industrial premises is not handled constantly, so checks are less frequent than for movable items. The recommended user-check interval here is weekly.

questions.prompt: When conducting insulation resistance tests on new household appliances with Class I insulation, the minimum value would be:
questions.explanation: For new Class I household appliances, the insulation resistance should be at least 1.0 megohm. That shows adequate separation between live parts and accessible earthed metal.

questions.prompt: There is no provision for protective earthing for which one of the following equipment:
questions.explanation: Class II equipment has no protective earth provision. It relies on double or reinforced insulation instead of installation earthing.

questions.prompt: Equipment found to be faulty must be:

options.C: Labelled, reported and withdrawn from service

questions.explanation: Faulty equipment must be made unavailable, clearly identified and escalated. Labelling, reporting and withdrawal from service prevents continued use before repair or disposal.

questions.prompt: Of the following items of information, which one is not required on a test label:

options.A: Date the test was carried out
options.C: Information on whether the equipment has passed or failed the safety tests

questions.explanation: A test label normally shows the item status and relevant test information such as date or next due date. Detailed previous results belong in the records, not on the appliance label.

questions.prompt: The scope of the EWR regarding maintenance of electrical systems extends to distribution systems up to:
questions.explanation: The Electricity at Work Regulations cover electrical systems broadly, including high-voltage distribution systems. In this mock the stated upper distribution scope is 400 kV.

questions.prompt: A fridge freezer is classified as:
questions.explanation: A fridge freezer is normally installed in one position and not moved during operation. Its mass and use make it a stationary appliance.

questions.prompt: The Code of Practice for In-service Inspection and Testing of Electrical Equipment does not apply to:
questions.explanation: Petrol station forecourts are specialised hazardous areas with additional controls for flammable atmospheres. They fall outside the normal in-service appliance Code of Practice scope.

questions.prompt: An insulation resistance tester should be capable of:

options.A: Maintaining the test voltage when applied to the equipment insulation
options.B: Supplying a maximum current of 0.5 A through the load
options.C: Supplying a minimum voltage of 1000 V d.c. to the load
options.D: Testing the continuity of a circuit

questions.explanation: An insulation resistance tester must hold the required test voltage while connected to the appliance insulation. Otherwise the reading would not prove the insulation at the specified test stress.

questions.prompt: Safety isolating transformers supplying Class III equipment must conform to:
questions.explanation: Class III equipment is supplied from a safety isolating transformer. BS 3535 is the transformer standard referenced for that SELV supply arrangement.

questions.prompt: When conducting an insulation resistance test on an electrical appliance the voltage supplied should be:
questions.explanation: The standard insulation resistance test for many appliances uses 500 V d.c. DC is used so the insulation resistance can be measured without normal AC load effects.

questions.prompt: When assessing the level of safety of an electrical appliance the most important check would be:
questions.explanation: Visual inspection is the key safety check because it finds the common real-world defects first. Instrument tests cannot compensate for obvious physical damage or misuse.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following checks should the user of an appliance be competent to undertake:

options.C: Tests using a portable appliance tester
options.D: Visual inspection of the flexible lead and plug

questions.explanation: A user check should be limited to visible condition, such as the flexible lead and plug. It is intended to catch obvious damage before the appliance is used.

questions.prompt: During a formal visual inspection a check should be made to confirm that the equipment is being operated:
questions.explanation: Formal visual inspection verifies that the appliance is being used as intended. Manufacturer's instructions define safe operation, ventilation, environment and loading.

questions.prompt: To which one of the following workplace environments does the IEE Code of Practice not apply:
questions.explanation: Specialised work situations can require extra standards and risk controls beyond the general appliance Code of Practice. The Code is aimed at normal in-service electrical equipment.

questions.prompt: The legal requirement for electrical equipment to be maintained in good order is laid down in the:

options.B: Health and Safety at Work Act 1974
options.C: Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999
options.D: Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations 1998

questions.explanation: The Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 impose the legal duty to maintain electrical systems and equipment to prevent danger. That is why they are the legal source for maintenance requirements.

questions.prompt: Instrument test leads should comply with:
questions.explanation: GS 38 gives the HSE requirements for safe voltage test leads and probes. Compliant leads reduce the chance of exposed tips, poor insulation or unsuitable fusing.

questions.prompt: The initial frequency of formal visual inspection for Class II cleaning equipment used in a school is recommended to be:
questions.explanation: School cleaning equipment is moved, flexed and used in a tougher environment than fixed office equipment. For Class II cleaning equipment in schools, the initial formal visual interval is 4 months.

questions.prompt: The test current applied to an electric kettle fitted with a 13A fuse during an earth continuity test would normally be:

options.C: 25A for a period between 5 and 20 seconds

questions.explanation: An electric kettle with a 13 A plug fuse is tested with the normal high-current earth continuity value. 25 A for 5 to 20 seconds verifies the protective conductor path under a demanding condition.

questions.prompt: Where a supply lead is tested separately, which one of the following is not applicable:

options.A: Earth continuity for a two core supply cord
options.B: Inspection and earth continuity test for a 3 core supply cord

questions.explanation: A two-core supply cord has no protective conductor. With no earth conductor present, an earth continuity test cannot apply.

questions.prompt: A continuous metal enclosure surrounding Class I equipment, would be classified as:
questions.explanation: A continuous metal enclosure is described as metal-cased. On Class I equipment that metal case is connected to the protective conductor for fault protection.

questions.prompt: If a standard 13 A plug became overheated the probability is that:

options.A: An incorrectly rated cartridge fuse is being used
options.B: Reversed polarity of the phase and earth conductors has occurred
options.D: There is a loose connection at one of the terminals

questions.explanation: Overheating at a 13 A plug is most commonly caused by a loose terminal. The poor connection creates resistance and heat when current flows.

questions.prompt: The length of a 1.25 mm² extension lead fitted with a standard 13 A plug should not be greater than:
questions.explanation: For a 1.25 mm² extension lead on a standard 13 A plug, the maximum length is 12 m. The limit helps control volt drop and earth fault loop impedance.

questions.prompt: Ohmmeters which are used to measure the resistance of an earth continuity conductor, must produce a short-circuit current between:
questions.explanation: Low resistance ohmmeters for earth continuity use a small test current. The required short-circuit current range is 20 mA to 200 mA.

questions.prompt: The length of a 1.5 mm² extension lead should not exceed:
questions.explanation: A 1.5 mm² extension lead should not exceed 15 m in this Code of Practice context. Longer leads increase volt drop and fault-loop impedance.

questions.prompt: Equipment with an earth leakage current designed to exceed 3.5 mA shall:

options.A: Be permanently wired or supplied by a plug and socket to BS4343 (BS EN 6030-2)
options.B: Have a label indicating the value of leakage current
options.C: Have protective conductors of not less than 0.5 mm² c.s.a

questions.explanation: Where equipment is designed to leak more than 3.5 mA to earth, the protective conductor must be especially reliable. Permanent connection or an industrial plug-and-socket arrangement provides that reliability.

questions.prompt: Generally speaking, the safety and correct functioning of portable appliances and equipment depends on the integrity of the fixed installation. Requirements for the inspection and testing of fixed installations are given in:
questions.explanation: Portable equipment may depend on the fixed installation for earthing and supply protection. Inspection and testing requirements for fixed installations are covered by BS 7671.

questions.prompt: Stationary equipment and appliances are defined as not having a carrying handle and have a mass exceeding:
questions.explanation: Stationary appliances are not provided with a carrying handle and exceed the movable-equipment mass threshold. The threshold used here is over 18 kg.

questions.prompt: The first test to be applied to an item of Class I equipment is:
questions.explanation: For Class I equipment, the protective conductor must be proven before other electrical tests or energising. Earth continuity is therefore the first electrical test.

questions.prompt: Equipment having no provision for the connection of exposed metalwork to a protective conductor is:
questions.explanation: Class II equipment has no protective earth connection because shock protection is by double or reinforced insulation. Exposed metal, if present, is not connected to a CPC for fault protection.

questions.prompt: Current flowing through a human body when it touches an accessible part is known as:
questions.explanation: Touch current is the current that could pass through a person touching an accessible part. It is the practical leakage current relevant to shock risk.

questions.prompt: Moveable (transportable) equipment is limited to a maximum mass of:
questions.explanation: Moveable or transportable equipment can be moved from place to place but is limited by mass. The maximum mass used for this classification is 18 kg.

questions.prompt: Which of the following tests assesses compliance with Bs or BS EN Standards:
questions.explanation: Type testing is carried out to prove that a product design complies with the relevant BS or BS EN standard. Routine PAT does not re-type-test the product design.

questions.prompt: Damaged equipment must be assessed as to suitability for use by:
questions.explanation: Damaged equipment needs a decision by the responsible person because they control repair, withdrawal or replacement. Users should report damage rather than decide continued use on their own.

questions.prompt: Low resistance ohmmeters must provide an open-circuit voltage no greater than:
questions.explanation: A low resistance ohmmeter must use a safe open-circuit voltage. The maximum stated value is 24 V.

questions.prompt: Which of the following checks/tests does not need to be recorded:
questions.explanation: Satisfactory user checks are informal and normally do not require a written record. Defects found during user checks should still be reported and acted on.

questions.prompt: No unprotected cables may be run:
questions.explanation: Running unprotected cables under carpets hides damage and can trap heat. It also exposes the cable to crushing and abrasion without being visible.

questions.prompt: 3A fuses may be used in plug tops for appliances up to:
questions.explanation: At 230 V, 700 W draws just over 3 A. A 3 A plug fuse is therefore suitable only up to about this load in the context of the mock.

questions.prompt: Flexible cables should be inspected for damage:

options.A: At the ends by visual inspection
options.B: At the ends by visual inspection and touch
options.C: Throughout its length by visual inspection
options.D: Throughout its length by visual inspection and touch

questions.explanation: Flexible cable damage can occur anywhere along the lead. Visual inspection and touch along the full length helps find cuts, crushing, kinks and heat damage.

questions.prompt: The length of a 1.5mm² should not exceed:
questions.explanation: For a 1.5 mm² extension lead, the maximum length used here is 15 m. This controls volt drop and ensures fault protection remains effective.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is correct regarding 13A plugs:

options.A: All pins must be partially insulated
options.B: All plugs must have insulated pins
options.C: New plugs must have live pins insulated
options.D: New plugs must have live pins partially insulated

questions.explanation: New BS 1363 plugs must have partially insulated line and neutral pins. The sleeving reduces access to live metal during insertion and removal.

questions.prompt: Before conducting testing on IT equipment:

options.B: Permission from the user is required
options.C: The socket circuit must be isolated

questions.explanation: IT equipment can be sensitive to testing and may be in active use. Permission from the user avoids data loss, interruption or unintended damage.

questions.prompt: The maximum protective conductor/touch current allowed for portable hand-held Class I equipment is:
questions.explanation: Portable hand-held Class I equipment has a low touch-current limit because it is held directly by the user. The maximum value stated here is 0.75 mA.

questions.prompt: Internal protective conductors of equipment designed to have a protective conductor current exceeding 3.5 mA should be not less than:
questions.explanation: Equipment designed for protective conductor current above 3.5 mA needs a robust internal earth path. A minimum 1.0 mm² internal protective conductor helps carry that current reliably.

questions.prompt: A plug connected to equipment with a rating of 1.5 kW should have a fuse rated at:
questions.explanation: A 1.5 kW appliance draws about 6.5 A at 230 V. The suitable standard BS 1362 plug fuse above that load is 13 A.

questions.prompt: Microwave ovens should be functionally tested to:

options.A: Check for leakage of radiation when the door is open
options.B: Check the value of the touch current
options.C: Ensure that opening the oven door breaks the power supply
options.D: Ensure the integrity of the insulation resistance

questions.explanation: The microwave door interlock must disconnect the power when the door is opened. Functional testing checks that this safety function operates correctly.

questions.prompt: An appliance which has double insulation throughout and also provision for earthing would be classified as what type of equipment:
questions.explanation: If the appliance provides an earthing connection, it is treated as Class I for protection purposes. The protective conductor arrangement must therefore be inspected and tested.

questions.prompt: Stationary equipment in schools would require user checks:
questions.explanation: Stationary equipment in schools has a lower handling risk than portable or handheld items but still needs routine user checks. The interval used here is weekly.

questions.prompt: If equipment gives suspect results during an insulation resistance test an alternative test would be a:
questions.explanation: If insulation resistance results are suspect or the test may be unsuitable, a protective conductor or touch-current test can be used instead. It assesses leakage under operating conditions.

questions.prompt: If manufacturers test procedures are not available and there is doubt which of the following tests should not be carried out:
questions.explanation: When manufacturer procedures are unavailable and there is doubt, an insulation test should not be applied. The test voltage may damage sensitive components or give misleading results.

questions.prompt: The maximum current carrying capacity of a 1.5 mm² cable is approximately:
questions.explanation: A 1.5 mm² flexible cable has an approximate current-carrying capacity of 15 A in this context. That is why it suits normal 13 A plug-connected loads within limits.

questions.prompt: 10 A is equal to:
questions.explanation: One kiloampere is 1000 amperes. Therefore 10 A is 10 / 1000 = 0.01 kA.

questions.prompt: When testing basic insulation the test connection points will be between:
questions.explanation: For a basic insulation test, line and neutral are joined together and tested against earth. That checks insulation between live conductors and accessible earthed parts.

questions.prompt: Which of the following situations regarding 'electrical equipment' is not covered by the Electricity at Work Regulations:

options.D: Employers equipment used for work at home

questions.explanation: The Electricity at Work Regulations apply to work activities and electrical systems at work. An employee's own equipment used only at home is outside that workplace scope.

questions.prompt: Which of the following should not influence a decision on how often equipment inspection and testing should take place:
questions.explanation: Inspection and test frequency is risk-based, considering use, environment, equipment type and users. Cost should not reduce the frequency needed to control danger.

questions.prompt: An earth continuity test should be carried out using a test current of between:

options.A: 1.5 times the fuse rating and 26 A
options.C: Twice the fuse rating and 20 A
options.D: Twice the fuse rating and 200 mA

questions.explanation: A high-current earth continuity test should be strong enough to prove the protective path. The value is between 1.5 times the fuse rating and a maximum of 26 A.

questions.prompt: Training may be required to ensure appliance users are able to carry out:
questions.explanation: Users may need training so they can carry out simple user checks and report defects promptly. That catches obvious faults between formal inspections.

questions.prompt: An insulation resistance test on Class I equipment indicates a result of 0.4 MΩ. When connected to a 230V supply the earth leakage current will be:
questions.explanation: Using Ohm's law, I = V/R = 230 V / 0.4 megohm. That equals about 0.00057 A, or 0.57 mA.

questions.prompt: Protective conductor currents exceeding 10 mA are unavoidable when using some equipment. In this case special precautions are required. Additional specific information regarding these precautions can be found in:
questions.explanation: Protective conductor currents above 10 mA need special installation precautions. BS 7671 gives the detailed requirements for those protective conductor arrangements.

questions.prompt: If an appliance has a detachable cord set, a test should be carried out on the appliance

options.C: With the cord set plugged in
options.D: Without the cord set plugged in

questions.explanation: A detachable cord set should be fitted when the appliance is tested so the item is checked as it is used. This also proves the inlet, cord and connections together.

questions.prompt: When testing microwave ovens, a check should be made that the warnings concerning microwave energy specified in BS EN 60335-2-25 are:

options.A: Included in the Equipment Instruction Book
options.B: Marked on the relevant covers of the appliance
options.C: Noted in the Equipment Register, Form Va
options.D: Noted on the Equipment Label, Form Vc

questions.explanation: Microwave warning labels must be on the relevant covers so anyone removing them sees the hazard notice. This helps prevent exposure to microwave energy during service or repair.

questions.prompt: Where equipment has a protective conductor current designed to exceed 3.5 mA, one requirement is that a label is fixed adjacent to the equipment primary power connection which includes the wording
questions.explanation: Equipment with designed high protective conductor current must warn users and maintainers at the point of connection. The required wording is Warning High Touch Current.

questions.prompt: Class II equipment may be constructed with

options.A: Earthed metalwork separated from live parts by basic insulation only
options.B: Exposed conductive parts connected to the main earthing terminal
options.C: Unearthed metalwork separated from live parts by basic and supplementary insulation
options.D: Unearthed metalwork separated from live parts by basic insulation only

questions.explanation: Class II protection can include unearthed accessible metalwork. It is acceptable only where basic and supplementary insulation separate that metalwork from live parts.

questions.prompt: The term 'equipment construction' relates to

options.A: How the user of equipment is protected against electric shock
options.B: The degree of protection offered against the ingress of moisture or water
options.C: The equipment's suitability for use within specific environmental conditions
options.D: Whether the equipment is hand-held, portable, movable or fixed in use

questions.explanation: Equipment construction describes the method used to protect the user from electric shock. The class of equipment is based on that protective construction.

questions.prompt: One purpose of carrying out an earth continuity test, using a low current ohmmeter, on equipment which relies on functional earthing is to ensure that the

options.A: Earthing allows the equipment to operate correctly
options.B: Equipment conforms to the requirements of BS 7822
options.C: Means of isolation from the supply are accessible

questions.explanation: Functional earthing may be needed for screening or correct operation rather than shock protection. The continuity test confirms that functional earth path is present.

questions.prompt: When conducting an earth continuity test on equipment that has accessible metal parts, which are earthed only for functional/screening purposes, these parts should be

options.A: Subjected to a measured touch current test
options.B: Tested at a current 1.5 times the fuse rating
options.C: Tested at a current between 20 mA to 200 mA
options.D: Tested for earth continuity at full current

questions.explanation: Accessible parts earthed only for functional or screening purposes should be tested gently. A 20 mA to 200 mA test avoids applying a high fault-current test to sensitive circuits.

questions.prompt: Portable appliance testers may, in some cases, be used for earth continuity testing using a low value of test current, typically
questions.explanation: A soft earth-continuity test uses a low test current, typically about 100 mA. It is useful where a high-current test could damage electronic equipment.

questions.prompt: Whilst carrying out an earth continuity measurement on a 3 kW Class I electric fire, the measured resistance slightly increases during the period of test. One possible reason for this increase in resistance could be

options.A: A loose connection at the earth terminal within the mains plug
options.B: An open circuit in the protective conductor
options.C: Degradation of the insulation due to an excessive test current
options.D: Insufficient current supplied by the test equipment

questions.explanation: A resistance that rises during a high-current test suggests heating at a poor connection. A loose earth terminal in the plug is a likely cause.

questions.prompt: The main purpose of the cartridge fuse fitted within a standard 13 A plug is to protect the appliance
questions.explanation: The BS 1362 cartridge fuse in a 13 A plug primarily protects the flexible cord set. It disconnects before the cord is damaged by excessive current.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is a statutory document?
questions.explanation: The Electricity at Work Regulations are statutory because they are law. Guidance documents and standards may support compliance, but they are not themselves statutory regulations.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following regulations states: 'Every employer shall make a suitable and sufficient assessment of the risk to the health and safety of his employees and to persons not in his employment'?

options.C: The Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations
options.D: The Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations

questions.explanation: That wording is the risk-assessment duty from the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations. It requires employers to assess risks to employees and others affected by the work.

questions.prompt: Certain sections of The Health and Safety at Work Regulations put a duty of care upon:

options.A: Both employees and the general public

questions.explanation: Health and safety law places duties on both sides of the workplace relationship. Employers must provide safe systems, and employees must take reasonable care and cooperate.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following regulations state: 'As may be necessary to prevent danger, all systems shall be maintained so as to prevent, so far as is reasonably practicable, such danger'?

options.C: The Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations
options.D: The Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations

questions.explanation: The quoted maintenance duty is from the Electricity at Work Regulations. Electrical systems must be maintained as necessary to prevent danger so far as reasonably practicable.

questions.prompt: The scope of legislation of inspection and testing of electrical equipment extends to distribution systems up to:
questions.explanation: The legislation covers electrical systems across the supply chain, including high-voltage distribution. The scope stated in this mock extends to 400 kV systems.

questions.prompt: The Code of Practice for In-service Inspection and Testing of Electrical Equipment does not apply to:
questions.explanation: Petrol station forecourts involve flammable atmospheres and specialist hazardous-area controls. They are outside the normal appliance in-service Code of Practice scope.

questions.prompt: The safety and proper functioning of certain portable appliances and equipment depends on the integrity of the fixed installation. Requirements for the inspecting and testing of fixed installations are given in:
questions.explanation: Portable equipment can depend on the fixed installation for earthing and supply protection. Fixed installation inspection and testing is covered by BS 7671.

questions.prompt: An electric kettle is classified as a:
questions.explanation: An electric kettle is plug-connected by a flexible cord and can be moved for normal use. That makes it a portable appliance in this classification.

questions.prompt: Which one-of the following domestic electrical appliances may be regarded as an item of stationary equipment?
questions.explanation: A washing machine is normally installed in one position and not moved while in use. Its weight and use make it stationary equipment.

questions.prompt: A portable appliance that is supplied by a flexible cord incorporating a protective conductor, is classified as:
questions.explanation: A flexible cord containing a protective conductor means the appliance relies on earthing for fault protection. That construction is Class I.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following arrangements would not meet the requirements of the lEE Code of Practice?

options.A: Class I equipment supplied by a 1.5 mm² three-core extension lead connected into a 13 A three-pin socket outlet
options.B: Class I equipment supplied by a 2.5 mm² three-core extension lead connected into a BS EN 60309-2 socket outlet
options.C: Class II equipment supplied by a 1.5 mm² two-core extension lead connected into a 13 A three-pin socket outlet
options.D: Class III equipment supplied by a two-core flexible cord connected into the secondary of an isolating transformer supplying SELV lighting equipment

questions.explanation: A two-core extension lead ending in a 13 A socket would not provide an earth to any Class I appliance later plugged into it. A 13 A socket outlet extension must preserve the protective conductor path.

questions.prompt: During the inspection and testing process, which of the following is not required:

options.A: Earth continuity test on Class II equipment
options.B: Earth continuity tests (for Class I equipment)

questions.explanation: Class II equipment has no protective conductor to test. Earth continuity testing is required for Class I equipment, not for Class II equipment.

questions.prompt: Details of which of the following must be recorded when carrying out a safety check on an electrical appliance:

options.D: User check revealing no damage to equipment

questions.explanation: A combined inspection and test produces formal safety results that must be recorded. The record links the appliance identity, test outcome and next review logic.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following will not affect the frequency of inspection and testing for an electrical appliance:

options.A: Environment in which it is to be used
options.C: The integrity of the fixed electrical installation

questions.explanation: Appliance inspection frequency is based on the appliance risk: use, environment, class and user behaviour. The fixed installation's condition is assessed separately under BS 7671.

questions.prompt: The suggested frequency for user checks for children's rides in a fairground is:
questions.explanation: Children's rides are high-use items used by vulnerable users and often in public areas. Daily user checks help catch obvious damage or misuse quickly.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following tests should not be applied routinely to equipment:
questions.explanation: Dielectric strength testing applies a high stress voltage and can damage insulation if used unnecessarily. It is not a routine in-service PAT test.

questions.prompt: The first electrical test to be applied to Class I equipment is:
questions.explanation: For Class I equipment, the earth path must be proven before other electrical tests. Earth continuity confirms exposed metalwork can clear a fault safely.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following items of information is not required on an inspection and test label?

options.A: An indication of whether the equipment has passed or failed the safety tests

questions.explanation: Inspection labels need current status information, not the full history. Details of previous test results should be kept in the test records.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is not required to be tested within the scope of the IEE Code of Practice?
questions.explanation: Fixed installations are inspected and tested under BS 7671. The appliance Code of Practice covers in-service electrical equipment, not the installation wiring itself.

questions.prompt: The Memorandum of Guidance on the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989 advises that equipment records:

options.A: Are not required if the equipment is fed from a 110 V safety supply
options.B: Are not required where the equipment is used in low-risk areas
options.C: Only be. kept where the equipment is used in high-risk areas
options.D: Should be kept throughout the working life of the equipment

questions.explanation: Equipment records support trend checks, retest intervals and duty-holder control. Keeping them for the working life of the equipment preserves that history.

questions.prompt: The person responsible for carrying out an inspection and test on an appliance should have made available to them:

options.A: A copy of the Electricity at Work Regulations
options.B: A copy of the Health and Safety at Work Act
options.C: A list of all. the users of equipment

questions.explanation: Previous results show the appliance history and can reveal deterioration or repeated faults. They also help decide whether the current inspection frequency is suitable.

questions.prompt: Which voltage must be used when carrying out an insulation resistance test on a Class I toaster?
questions.explanation: A Class I toaster is normally insulation-tested at 500 V d.c. This checks insulation between live parts and accessible earthed metal.

questions.prompt: An insulation resistance tester should be capable of:

options.A: Delivering a maximum voltage of 25 A through the load
options.B: Delivering a minimum voltage of 1000 V d.c. to the load
options.C: Maintaining the test voltage required across the load
options.D: Testing the continuity of an earthing circuit

questions.explanation: The tester must maintain the required voltage while connected to the insulation being tested. If the voltage collapses, the measured resistance is not meaningful.

questions.prompt: Where a user check reveals damage to equipment, it must be reported to:

options.A: A manager of an inspection and test organization

questions.explanation: A damaged item found by a user must be escalated to the responsible person. That person can arrange withdrawal, repair, replacement and recording.

questions.prompt: The manager of an inspection and test organisation should be able to:

options.A: Demonstrate competence in the use of appliance testers
options.B: Instruct untrained persons in the use of portable appliance testers
options.C: Know their legal responsibilities under the Electricity at Work Regulations

questions.explanation: The manager must understand the legal duties that govern inspection and testing work. The Electricity at Work Regulations set core responsibilities for preventing electrical danger.

questions.prompt: Earth continuity testing may in certain circumstances be carried out by means of:

options.C: An instrument complying with BS EN 60309

questions.explanation: A low resistance ohmmeter can be used to measure the protective conductor path where appropriate. It is suited to small resistance values in continuity checks.

questions.prompt: Test leads and probes used to measure voltages over 50 V a.c. and 100 V d.c. should comply with:

options.A: BS 5490 Specification for classification of Protection
options.C: Health & Safety Executive Guidance Note GS38

questions.explanation: GS38 is the HSE guidance for safe test leads and probes. It covers features such as insulation, finger guards and exposed tip length.

questions.prompt: Where protection against electric shock from equipment is provided using a protective conductor in the fixed wiring, the equipment classification would be:
questions.explanation: Protection by a protective conductor in the fixed wiring is Class I protection. The earth path allows fault current from exposed metalwork to operate the protective device.

questions.prompt: A substantially continuous metal enclosure associated with Class II equipment would be classified as:
questions.explanation: A substantially continuous metal enclosure is described as metal-cased. In Class II equipment that metalwork remains unearthed but separated from live parts by suitable insulation.

questions.prompt: There is no provision for protective earthing or reliance upon installation conditions for which one of the following equipment?
questions.explanation: Class II equipment has no protective earth provision and does not rely on installation earthing. It relies on double or reinforced insulation for shock protection.

questions.prompt: Which voltage should be applied when conducting an insulation resistance test on an electrical appliance?
questions.explanation: The normal insulation resistance test voltage for appliances in this context is 500 V d.c. It stresses the insulation enough to reveal weakness without using the AC supply.

questions.prompt: User checks of stationary equipment installed in industrial premises should be conducted:
questions.explanation: Stationary industrial equipment is not moved constantly, but it still needs routine visible checks. The user-check interval stated here is weekly.

questions.prompt: During a formal visual inspection it should be confirmed that the equipment is being operated:
questions.explanation: Formal visual inspection includes confirming the appliance is used as the maker intended. Manufacturer's instructions define correct loading, environment, ventilation and operation.

questions.prompt: If a standard 13 A plug became overheated the most likely cause would be:

options.A: A loose connection at one or more of the terminals
options.C: Reversed polarity of the cable conductors
options.D: The use of an incorrectly rated cartridge fuse

questions.explanation: A loose plug terminal creates resistance at the connection. Load current through that resistance produces heat, making it the most likely cause of overheating.

questions.prompt: When conducting insulation resistance tests on new household electrical appliances to BS 3456 Class I insulation, the minimum value would be:
questions.explanation: For new Class I household appliances, the minimum insulation resistance is 1.0 megohm in this test context. That confirms adequate separation between live conductors and earthed accessible parts.

questions.prompt: An ohmmeter used to measure the resistance of an earth continuity conductor, must be capable of producing a short-circuit current between:
questions.explanation: A low resistance ohmmeter for this continuity test must deliver a short-circuit current in the 20 mA to 200 mA range. That is enough for measurement without a high-current stress test.

questions.prompt: An insulation resistance test of a Class I household portable appliance is to be carried out. using the earth leakage method. The maximum acceptable value is:
questions.explanation: The earth leakage method measures current flowing to earth under the test condition. For this Class I household appliance case, the maximum accepted leakage is 0.75 mA.

questions.prompt: Equipment found to be faulty must not be used but must be:

options.C: Labelled, reported and withdrawn from service

questions.explanation: Faulty equipment must not remain available for use. Labelling, reporting and withdrawal ensure the hazard is clear and the responsible person can arrange action.

questions.prompt: IT equipment which is not constructed to BS EN 60950 may be damaged by an applied voltage insulation resistance test. The test that should replace it is:
questions.explanation: Some IT equipment can be damaged by a 500 V insulation resistance test. An earth leakage test checks safety by measuring leakage current instead.

questions.prompt: Equipment with an earth leakage current designed to exceed 3.5 mA shall:

options.A: Be permanently wired or supplied by a plug and socket to BS 4343 (BS EN 6030-2)
options.B: Have a label permanently fixed indicating the value of leakage current
options.C: Have internal protective conductors of not less than 0.5 mm² c.s.a
options.D: Only be used in industrial situations

questions.explanation: Designed leakage above 3.5 mA requires a secure protective conductor connection. Permanent wiring or an industrial plug-and-socket arrangement reduces the risk of losing the earth path.

questions.prompt: In order to reduce the possibility of electric shock through contact with live parts, the aperture of any electrical equipment must

options.A: Be located so as to be inaccessible to the user
options.B: Be subjected to dielectric strength testing
options.C: Comply with the requirements of BS EN 50950
options.D: Meet test finger and test pin requirements

questions.explanation: Apertures must prevent access to live parts by standard test fingers and pins. Passing those tests shows the enclosure gives effective basic protection.

questions.prompt: For protection against electric shock, Class III equipment relies upon a supply derived from a
questions.explanation: Class III equipment relies on SELV for shock protection. The supply must be separated from higher-voltage circuits so dangerous voltage cannot appear at the equipment.

questions.prompt: Class II equipment may be constructed with

options.A: Earthed metalwork separated from live parts by basic and supplementary insulation
options.B: Earthed metalwork separated from live parts by basic insulation only
options.C: Unearthed metalwork separated from live parts by basic and supplementary insulation
options.D: Unearthed metalwork separated from live parts by basic insulation only

questions.explanation: Class II equipment can include unearthed metal parts. Those parts are safe only because basic and supplementary insulation separate them from live parts.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following types of equipment in shops and offices is considered the most likely to develop dangerous faults?
questions.explanation: Hand-held equipment is gripped, moved and flexed during use, so damage is more likely to become dangerous. Its lead, casing and strain relief are under more stress than stationary equipment.

questions.prompt: When conducting a formal visual inspection on equipment used outdoor, it is important that the equipment has a suitable
questions.explanation: Outdoor equipment must resist ingress from its environment. The IP rating tells the inspector whether the enclosure is suitable for dust and water exposure.

questions.prompt: If an inspector considers that the equipment being tested is not suitable for the environment, this should be

options.A: Recorded after the operative has been instructed as to the possible danger
options.B: Recorded and brought to the attention of the responsible person
options.C: Reported to the Health & Safety Executive
options.D: Reported to the manufacturer of the equipment

questions.explanation: Unsuitability for the environment is a safety finding that must be recorded. It also needs to be brought to the responsible person's attention so corrective action can be taken.

questions.prompt: Prior to applying insulation resistance tests to electrical equipment, the

options.A: Fuses should be checked, switches in the OFF position and all covers removed if possible
options.B: Fuses should be checked, switches in the ON position and covers in place
options.C: Switches should be in the OFF position and all covers in place
options.D: Switches should be in the ON position and all covers removed if possible

questions.explanation: Before insulation testing, switches should be on so internal circuits are included, while covers stay in place for safety. Fuses should also be checked so the test path is complete.

questions.prompt: When conducting an earth continuity test on equipment that has accessible metal parts, which are earthed only for functional/screening purposes, these parts should be

options.A: Subjected to a measured touch current test
options.B: Tested at a circuit 1.5 times the fuse rating
options.C: Tested at a current between 20 mA to 200mA
options.D: Tested for earth continuity at full current

questions.explanation: Parts earthed only for functional or screening purposes should be tested with a low current. The 20 mA to 200 mA range avoids applying a high-current earth test to sensitive circuits.

questions.prompt: When using certain types of test instrument, as an alternative to subtracting the lead resistance from the final measured value, the lead resistance may be
questions.explanation: Nulling compensates for the resistance of the test leads before measuring the appliance. It avoids having to subtract the lead resistance manually from the final reading.

questions.prompt: When applying a test voltage to an item of Class I equipment, a value of 0.1 MO is obtained. One possible reason for this low reading could be

options.A: A short circuit between live conductors within the appliance cord set
options.B: An open circuit has occurred within the protective conductor
options.C: Progressive failure of the insulation between live conductors
options.D: Progressive failure of the insulation between live conductors and earth

questions.explanation: A very low insulation reading between live conductors and earth points to insulation breakdown to the earthed parts. Progressive failure of live-to-earth insulation is therefore a likely cause.

questions.prompt: Equipment in which protection against electric shock relies on supply at SELV is:
questions.explanation: Class III equipment is protected by supply at separated extra-low voltage. It does not rely on earthing or double insulation as the main protective measure.

questions.prompt: The Electricity at Work Regulations came into force in:
questions.explanation: The Electricity at Work Regulations are the 1989 statutory regulations for electrical safety at work. They set duties to prevent danger from electrical systems and equipment.

questions.prompt: The most important check on a portable appliance is:
questions.explanation: Visual inspection is the most important PAT check because it finds common hazards before instruments are used. Damaged plugs, leads, cases and signs of overheating are often visible.

questions.prompt: The Code of Practice for in-service inspection recommends the initial frequency of combined inspection and testing on Class I IT equipment in schools should be:
questions.explanation: Class I IT equipment in schools has regular use and relies on a protective conductor. The initial combined inspection and test frequency used here is 12 months.

questions.prompt: PAT test instruments must be able to deliver an earth continuity test current up to a maximum of around:
questions.explanation: PAT instruments used for high-current earth continuity tests need to deliver about 25 A. That current proves the protective conductor path on equipment protected by a 13 A fuse.

questions.prompt: Low resistance ohmmeters must provide a test current within the range:
questions.explanation: Low resistance ohmmeters use a limited test current for continuity measurements. The required range is 20 mA to 200 mA.

questions.prompt: The length of a 1.5 mm² extension lead should not exceed:
questions.explanation: A 1.5 mm² extension lead is limited to 15 m in this context. The limit controls volt drop and ensures protective devices can still operate effectively.

questions.prompt: Formal visual inspections should be carried out by:
questions.explanation: A formal visual inspection requires competence because it involves judgement and may include checks users should not attempt. User checks are simpler and limited to obvious defects.

questions.prompt: Equipment that is permanently connected to a flex outlet type of accessory can be more easily tested using:

options.B: A dedicated portable appliance test instrument

questions.explanation: A permanently connected appliance cannot simply be plugged into a standard PAT tester. An insulation and continuity tester can test the fixed flex-outlet arrangement more practically.

questions.prompt: Which of the following tests may inadvertently damage equipment insulation:
questions.explanation: Dielectric strength testing applies a high test voltage to insulation. Used inappropriately, it can overstress or damage appliance insulation.

questions.prompt: The length of a 2.5mm² extension lead should not exceed:
questions.explanation: For a 2.5 mm² extension lead, the maximum length used here is 25 m. The larger conductor permits a longer lead while keeping impedance and volt drop under control.

questions.prompt: If the maximum length of an extension lead is exceeded it should be fitted with a:
questions.explanation: If an extension lead exceeds the recommended length, fault protection and shock risk become less favourable. A 30 mA RCD provides additional protection.

questions.prompt: The minimum cross-sectional area for a flex protected by a 3A fused BS 1363 plug is:
questions.explanation: A 3 A BS 1363 plug fuse can protect a 0.5 mm² flexible cord. Smaller conductors would not have adequate protection at that fuse rating.

questions.prompt: The current used for continuity testing on Class I equipment should have a range of:
questions.explanation: For the low-current continuity method on Class I equipment, the test current is 20 mA to 200 mA. This verifies the earth path without applying a high-current stress test.

questions.prompt: The most important test on Class I equipment is:
questions.explanation: Class I equipment depends on its protective conductor for fault protection. Earth continuity is therefore the key test to prove exposed metalwork can disconnect a fault safely.

questions.prompt: The definition 'A conductive part liable to introduce a potential, generally earth potential, and not forming part of the electrical installation' describes which of the following:
questions.explanation: An extraneous conductive part is conductive, can introduce earth potential, and is not part of the electrical installation. Pipework entering a building is a typical example.

questions.prompt: The maximum protective conductor/touch current allowed for Class II equipment is:
questions.explanation: Class II equipment has a very low permitted touch current because it has no protective earth. The maximum stated value is 0.25 mA.

questions.prompt: Equipment designed to have a protective conductor current exceeding 3.5 mA should:

options.B: Have a warning label fixed adjacent to the equipment primary power connection
options.C: Have an internal protective not less than 0.5 mm²
options.D: Have an internal protective not less than 0.75 mm²

questions.explanation: Equipment with protective conductor current above 3.5 mA must warn people at the supply connection. A fixed label near the primary power connection highlights the high touch-current condition.

questions.prompt: A plug connected to equipment with a rating of 300 W should have a fuse rated at:
questions.explanation: A 300 W appliance draws about 1.3 A at 230 V. A 3 A plug fuse is the appropriate standard rating above that load.

questions.prompt: The minimum acceptable value of insulation resistance for Class II equipment is:
questions.explanation: Class II equipment relies on double or reinforced insulation, so the insulation standard is higher than for some Class I cases. The minimum accepted value here is 2.0 megohms.

questions.prompt: Moveable equipment in industrial premises would be requiring user checks:
questions.explanation: Moveable equipment in industrial premises is exposed to frequent handling and harsher conditions. User checks before use help catch damage before it becomes dangerous.

questions.prompt: Overheating within a 13A plug would most likely be caused by:
questions.explanation: A loose connection creates resistance in the plug. Load current through that resistance produces heat, so it is the most likely cause of overheating.

questions.prompt: The requirements for testing fixed electrical installations supplying portable equipment are to be found in:
questions.explanation: Fixed installations supplying portable equipment are inspected and tested under BS 7671. PAT checks the appliance; BS 7671 covers the installation wiring and protective measures.

questions.prompt: The maximum current carrying capacity of a 1.0 mm² cable is approximately:
questions.explanation: In this context, a 1.0 mm² flexible cable has an approximate current-carrying capacity of 10 A. That guides suitable fuse and load selection.

questions.prompt: 1Ω is equal to:
questions.explanation: The prefix milli means one thousandth of the base unit. Rearranging that relationship, one full ohm contains 1000 milliohms.

questions.prompt: Which of the following construction classes may be used without special precautions being taken:
questions.explanation: Class I and Class II are the normal appliance construction classes accepted without the special concerns of Class 0 or 0I. Class III also depends on a suitable SELV supply arrangement.

questions.prompt: Which of the following procedures does not require a record to be kept:
questions.explanation: Routine user checks are informal and normally do not need a record when satisfactory. Inspection and testing activities need records because they support duty-holder control and retest planning.

questions.prompt: A review of inspection frequency can be assisted by referring to the:
questions.explanation: An equipment register shows what items exist, their type, location and history. That information helps review whether inspection intervals remain suitable.

questions.prompt: Training might be required on order that management understand their legal responsibilities as required by the:

options.B: IEE Guidance Note on inspection and testing
options.D: Provision and Use of Work Equipment Regulations

questions.explanation: Management must understand their legal duties to maintain electrical equipment safely. Those duties come from the Electricity at Work Regulations.

questions.prompt: In order to keep accurate records equipment used for testing should be:

options.C: Kept in a locked secure place

questions.explanation: Test records are only trustworthy if the instruments producing them remain accurate. Regular calibration proves the tester is giving reliable results.

questions.prompt: 10 mA converted to amperes is
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, 0.01 A is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: When carrying out a low or high current test, in both cases the protective conductor test should be made between accessible conductive paths and

options.D: The earth pin of the plug

questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, The earth pin of the plug is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: What test voltage is recommended when carrying out an insulation resistance test where surge protection devices are incorporated in the equipment?
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, 250 V d.c. is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Which regulations place a legal requirement on a landlord, who provides electrical equipment as part of a tenancy, to ensure that it is safe when first supplied?
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, The electrical equipment (safety) regulations is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: The health and safety executive provide guidance documents on maintaining electrical equipment. What publication provides guidance on electrical safety on construction sites?
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, HSG141 is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: A portable appliance is fitted with a cable 4.5m long and has a protective condor of 1.0mm2. Calculate the resistance of the protective conductor.
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, 87.75 milliohms is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: What is the frequency of testing for a mobile class 1 item of equipment used in commercial kitchens
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, There are no specified timescales is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: A load test is particularly useful for
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, Heating equipment is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: What causes high protective conductor currents in equipment such as variable speed drive which incorporates an EMC filter?

options.A: The capacitors and discharge resistors within the filter
options.B: The length of the CPC cable
options.C: The choke that is wired in series with the line conductor
options.D: The choke that is wired in series with the neutral conductor

questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, The capacitors and discharge resistors within the filter is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: When tested separately, a 2 core lead set is tested as a
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, Class II appliance is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: A method of reducing the risk of electric shock under fault conditions is to use SELV equipment, this method

options.A: Uses a centre tapped transformed with the centre connected to earth
options.C: Has no connection to earth on the load side
options.D: Needs to have an earth connection on the load side

questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, Has no connection to earth on the load side is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: A person who is not skilled in electrical work, but is classed as competent to carry out inspection and testing of electrical equipment, is known as being competent to which level?
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, Level 3 is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: What is not considered to be a factor when considering a risk based assessment when determining the initial frequency of inspection and testing?

options.C: The fixed wiring RCD trip time

questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, The fixed wiring RCD trip time is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: According to the Code of Practice which basic requirement demonstrates that a maintenance regime for electrical appliances exists within an organisation?

options.A: The records of inspections and tests
options.B: The invoices from the inspection and testing contractor
options.D: A kitemark logo on the company letterhead

questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, The records of inspections and tests is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Extension leads that are longer than the recommended lengths should be protected by a
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, 30mA RCD is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Equipment, in which protection against electric shock relies upon basic insulation only, is the definition of construction classification
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, Class 0 is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: A 2m length of flex with a csa of 0.75mm squared which has a rewireable plug top has a maximum fuse rating of
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, 6A is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: The sample test instrument record sheet provided in the Code of Practice requires certain details to be kept about the instruments used. These details include

options.A: Instrument Manufacturer; Model; Serial Number and Date of next calibration
options.B: Instrument type; Model; Serial Number and Date of last calibration
options.C: Instrument Manufacturer; Model; Serial Number and Date of last calibration
options.D: Instrument type; Model; Serial Number and Date of next calibration

questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, Instrument Manufacturer; Model; Serial Number and Date of last calibration is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Why must business equipment be powered down prior to disconnecting from the supply when undertaking formal inspection?

options.A: Fibre optic data cables will be safe to disconnect
options.B: There is a risk of data loss

questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, There is a risk of data loss is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: A toaster is generally classified as
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, Portable is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Which would not be carried out on Class II equipment?
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, Protective conductor continuity test is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Some aspects of a fixed installation, when noticed, should be recorded or discussed with the owner of the property. Which of these should not lead to a tester’s recommendation that the installation itself should be inspected or reviewed?

options.D: Red and black cores in the fixed wiring

questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, Red and black cores in the fixed wiring is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: When performance testing an RCD, the test should be done using
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, 30mA is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Which class of equipment is NOT acceptable in the UK?
questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, Class 0 is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: The dimensions of the conductors in an extension lead affect the resistance of the lead. Which of these correctly describes two conditions when resistance would reduce?

options.A: Increase in length and increase in diameter
options.B: Increase in diameter and reduction in length
options.C: Increase in length and reduction in diameter
options.D: Reduction in length and reduction in diameter

questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, Increase in diameter and reduction in length is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: A severe electric shock occur under fault free conditions if the body is placed between

options.A: The earth pin of a power socket and the metallic case of a class 1 item
options.B: Two conductors at the same potential

questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, A live conductor and earth is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: The electricity at work regulations is only one item of legislation which refers to electrical equipment used at work. The voltages covered by this legislation

options.A: Are anything above the domestic voltage of 230V
options.B: Range up to 1000V a.c. or 2500V d.c. between conductors
options.C: Range from extra low voltage battery powered items to 400kV transmission equipment
options.D: Are anything below 600V a.c. or 900V d.c. between conductors and earth

questions.explanation: Under the IET Code of Practice and electrical-equipment safety principles, Range from extra low voltage battery powered items to 400kV transmission equipment is the applicable answer for the stated conditions; the alternatives describe a different requirement, test condition, classification or unsafe outcome.

questions.prompt: Which of these does not describe a category of inspection and testing, referred to in the Code of Practice?
